headline: Federal Reserve officials now see the AI data centre boom as a key reason goods prices stay high.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: central bank minutes link AI spending to prices; the Washington Post report is read through a relay, the minutes were not read.
importance_line: US households and borrowers are affected because officials name AI spending as a reason prices stay high, yet the minutes show officials divided over why rates might need to rise and unsure how large AI's productivity gains will be.
summary: The Washington Post reports, as relayed by Newser, that minutes of the Fed's September meeting, released on Wednesday, rank the AI infrastructure boom above tariffs as a key force keeping goods prices elevated. The minutes also show officials divided over the reasons for raising interest rates, Reuters reports, and the Fed now expects inflation to stay above its 2% goal until 2029.
